reviewedAreas.conclusion: Allocation-only semantics are consistent with existing callers: cell Set insertion preserves order, empty traces skip only empty loops, and selfContact uses an owned shallow array without mutating its segment objects. Both callers complete contact selection synchronously before appendTrail mutates accepted tail endpoints. Contact arithmetic, horizons, failure ordering and accepted-trail mutation are unchanged.
reviewedAreas.limit: This is semantic inspection and passing focused boundary tests, not proof that every existing recording still reaches its terminal checkpoint on changed simulation bytes.

reviewedAreas.conclusion: Render-only cached backing recovery retains one surface per weak image/color cache entry. Lost surfaces are withheld; restoration marks them dirty and regenerates pixels. Failed readback removes the cache entry. Event closures retain the surface, not the source-image key; no document/global listener or simulation scheduler is introduced. Existing sprite placement and disc geometry remain unchanged.

Downloaded playback can reuse the current acquisition's inspector result only for the exact returned immutable Blob. The pinned asset comparison remains in source and playback, mismatched/custom-returned Blobs take ordinary validation, and generation/disposal/abort guards prevent retained callbacks installing stale work. Inspector abort listeners are removed in finally; no new persistence or music-intent writer is added.
Cancellation is checked after arrayBuffer resolves and before container parsing. The generated optional runtime reflects the same boundary. Ordinary media ownership remains unchanged.

Nested-tool return reveals only the already selected Settings panel, checks owner/visibility/focus eligibility, and otherwise returns to category focus. It does not step gameplay or change demo takeover ownership. The merged fullscreen implementation adds exactly the incoming focus behavior; its only distinct changed marker is independently reproduced from the four canonical sources.

The two conflict resolutions are generated-output changes. The official merged-locale i18n check passes without tracked changes, so the final catalog agrees with merged canonical locale sources; no generated conflict side is accepted as manually authoritative.

Require terminal outcome and meaningful capture progress for every clip, strict final checkpoint matching for qualified clips, and preserve failures without generating replacement outcomes.
